guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / major bleeding and shock
title: Severe crushed hand injury at a steam rally
setting: Vintage steam engine rally. A 42M exhibitor accidentally got his hand caught in the mechanism. Heavy arterial bleeding, mangled hand, in severe pain.
verdictExplanation: Mangled extremity with rapid, heavy arterial bleeding and early signs of shock (tachycardia 120 bpm, hypotension 87/57, pale skin). Sick: immediate bleed control and 999.

shared.danger: Mechanical steam engine gears (isolated and safe now)
shared.response: Alert but highly distressed, level of response dropping
shared.catHaem: Heavy, rapid bleeding from crushed hand
shared.circulation: Extremely fast pulse, cold, clammy, and pale skin

history.history: Hand caught in the gear mechanism of a running steam engine moments ago
history.injuries: Severe crush injury to lower hand and wrist, partial amputation of fingers
history.additional: Patient is in excruciating pain and highly panicked

followUp.question: What is your immediate priority action for this catastrophic haemorrhage?

options.text: Apply immediate firm direct pressure over a sterile dressing, elevate the hand, and call 999
Wash the wound thoroughly under warm running water to remove grease
Apply a tourniquet above the elbow immediately to stop catastrophic haemorrhage
Lie him flat on his stomach and tell him to rest his hand

followUp.explanation: Current JRCALC/SJA guidelines state that a tourniquet is the first-line treatment for catastrophic limb haemorrhage. Apply it firmly above the bleeding point. Washing the wound increases bleeding and should be avoided. Place him flat on his back (supine) to treat for shock, never on his stomach.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Apply firm direct pressure, elevate, call 999. Watch for signs of shock (sweating, cold clammy skin). Keep him warm.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected hemorrhagic shock. Apply pressure dressing. If bleeding cannot be controlled with direct pressure, immediately apply a commercial tourniquet above the wound, note the time, administer high-flow oxygen, keep warm, and expedite transport.
